newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Tech stock options busy on dip.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Tech stock options busy on dip.

text.p: Options on technology shares again were the favored play on Friday as some of the stocks were unable to maintain their Thursday rebound.
"I am a little confused," one trader said. "Tech stocks have been very weak. They've obviously had a correction, but maybe it's not over."
Specifically, he noted International Business Machines Corp and Intel Corp. IBM was down 4-1/8 at 132-3/4 and Intel lost 1-1/4 to 132.
"The whole thing that's holding the market down is Intel and IBM," the trader said.
IBM options were among the most active around. The two most active IBM options were the March 135 put and call, which traded 4,620 and 4,430 contracts, respectively.
Those options go off the boards Friday.
In the April series, the 125, 130, 135 and 140 puts were busy, as were the April 135, 140 and 145 calls.
The heaviest turnover in Intel options also was in the expiring March series, led by the 130 and 135 calls, which traded 2,500 and 2,600 contracts, respectively.

Intel options often top the most actives list at the American Stock Exchange, but on Friday that distinction was held by Ascend Communications Inc on the call side and Philip Morris Cos Inc on the put side.
The Ascend March 50 call traded about 3,950 contracts and the Philip Morris April 120 put traded 2,620.
Ascend shares, up 1-3/8 at 51-5/8, extended their rebound off 41-7/8 reached on Wednesday.
Philip Morris shares remained under pressure with the rest of the tobacco group after Brooke Group Ltd's Liggett Group settled tobacco litigation on Thursday.
The stock, which lost 6-1/8 points Thursday, was down another 5-3/8 at 110-1/2 on consolidated volume of 7.47 million shares Friday afternoon.

In other activity, options on shares of IVAX Corp were fairly busy after a slow morning after news late Thrusday that Bergen Brunswig Corp had terminated a previously announced $1.6 billion merger agreement with IVAX and planned to file a lawsuit alleging breach of the merger pact.
IVAX fell two to 10-3/8 and Bergen Brunswig rose 5/8 to 32-1/8.
Jon Najarian, president of Mercury Trading in Chicago, said the lack of much options activity in IVAX earlier was most likely because investors were attempting to digest the news.
"The deal is over and now the lawsuits start," he said.
Among the options, the IVAX March 12-1/2 put was most active, with turnover of 1,285 contracts.
Outside of the expiring March series, the September 12-1/2 put was most active, with volume of nearly 1,100 contracts. The June 10 puts and calls were also active.
